result.reviewScopeSummary: Verified Story 0 foundation deliverables against the story, the full Session Context Store tech design, and the test plan. Reviewed the package verification scripts, shared domain/error/id helpers, downstream test scaffolding, and the required `foundation.test.ts` coverage, then ran the targeted gate plus the story and epic gates.

newFindings.title: `deriveTargetSessionKeys` does not enforce the required realpath-based file key contract
newFindings.evidence: Story 0 makes `deriveTargetSessionKeys(...)` the shared association helper for later stories, and the tech design fixes file-based keys to `pi:session-file:<realpath(sessionFilePath)>` so one PI session cannot be associated twice through different file aliases (story `00-foundation.md` lines 95-97; tech design `Target Session Key Contract`, lines 595-603). In `src/context-steward/domain/ids.ts` lines 69-70 the default normalizer is `resolve()`, not `realpath()`. A direct repro with `node --import tsx` produced different canonical keys for the same session file and a symlink alias, so the helper still distinguishes aliases that should collapse to one canonical key. `tests/context-steward/foundation.test.ts` lines 23-32 only inject a fake normalizer and therefore do not verify the required default contract.

productionPathFindings: The default `deriveTargetSessionKeys` implementation uses `resolve()` instead of the design-required `realpath()` normalization, so production attach/start flows can generate different canonical file keys for the same PI session when the session file is reached through a symlink or alternate path alias.
additionalObservations: `npm run verify` and `npm run verify-all` both passed; `verify-all` reported `No integration tests found.`, which is consistent with Story 0's chunk-0 plan because this story only owns the two non-TC foundation tests.

Code inspection did not find early implementation of thread-store, capture, turn, import, repair, or fixture runtime behavior in the foundation modules; the surfaced blocker is confined to the shared target-key helper contract.
